hosting.//: 'main' is the project's original default site (voxmind-504022.web.app). Kept deploying, not decommissioned -- old bookmarks, anything cached, and any doc still pointing at that URL keeps working. 'cu' (voxmind-cu.web.app) is the nicer URL meant to actually be shared going forward. Both are the same free Spark-plan multi-site feature, no billing upgrade involved; `firebase deploy --only hosting` (unqualified) still deploys to both exactly as before this split, so nothing in the existing deploy habit changes.

headers.//: index.html must never be cached. Firebase's default is max-age=3600 for everything, and index.html is the file that names which hashed JS bundle to load -- so for an hour after every deploy, returning visitors kept loading the previous build and saw no changes at all. That is not a stale-content annoyance, it is a deploy that silently does nothing.

The opposite treatment for build assets: Vite fingerprints them with a content hash, so a given URL's contents can never change. Caching them for a year is safe and means a repeat visitor re-downloads only index.html.

Clickjacking matters more than usual here. This app asks for camera and microphone permission, and the classic attack is to frame the real site invisibly over a decoy so the victim clicks 'Allow' believing it belongs to another page.
Stops a browser from second-guessing a Content-Type and executing something served as data.
Send the full URL only to ourselves. Other origins get the bare origin, so a path that identifies a user or device never leaks in a Referer header.

The most valuable header for this project: camera and microphone are usable by this origin and denied to every embedded frame. Anything the page embeds is cut off from the sensors regardless of what it asks for.

hosting.//: cu: identical config to 'main', deliberately -- this is the same build, just also reachable at the nicer URL. Nothing here should ever drift from the block above; if you're editing headers/rewrites, edit both.
